- conv3: 32->64, 3x3 pad1, ReLU, MaxPool 2x2: 8x8 -> 8x8 -> 4x4

- fc: 64->10

A backdoor trigger near a corner (1 pixel in) would be at spatial positions near the corner of the input. After conv1 (3x3 pad1), the corner pixels still influence corner positions. After pooling, the corner region gets pooled.

The key insight for detecting backdoors from weights alone: A backdoored network often has a "detector" pathway. Then conv2/conv3 might propagate this, and finally fc would have a strong weight from some conv3 channel (which detects the trigger at a corner) to the target class.

However, with global average pooling, spatial information is lost! GAP averages over all 4x4 positions. So if a trigger is in one corner, after conv3+pool we get 4x4 feature maps, and GAP averages them. A trigger in one corner would activate only one spatial position (or a few) of the 4x4 map. After GAP, this signal is diluted by factor of 16.
